alive.last_commit_message:
Fix runtime prompt/resource scanning and LLM analysis for MCP bodies. (#257)

* Fix runtime prompt/resource scanning and LLM analysis for MCP bodies.

Fetch prompts/get message text and resources/read content into analyzers, enable YARA on resources, extend the shared threat prompt for resource/prompt bodies, and handle empty Bedrock completions without aborting scans.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Address CodeRabbit review for prompt and resource runtime scans.

Fail closed when prompts/get errors, bound concurrent prompt analysis, enforce effective MIME allowlists, fix PromptDefense entity naming, and clarify body-text prompt-injection criteria in the shared threat prompt.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Normalize resource MIME allowlist checks and keep prompt bodies on analysis failure.

Compare base MIME types case-insensitively and preserve prompt_messages_text when post-fetch analysis errors.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: keep generated prompt arguments out of the message body

_analyze_prompt appended Arguments: after Messages:, and the body
extractor returns everything after Messages:. Argument schema therefore
became part of Body. Splitting the body on the literal Arguments: is
unsafe because rendered messages can contain that sequence.

Emit arguments before Messages:. When a prompt has no Messages: section,
the extracted body is empty so metadata is not presented as message
text. Metadata-only prompts still reach analysis through their
description.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: enforce read MIME and bound prompt/resource scan work

A resources/list MIME type no longer overrides the type returned with the body, and prompt/resource collection stops at configurable size, count, and timeout budgets instead of reporting a complete scan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* fix: cover both resource APIs and keep analyzer payloads inside the budget

Early MIME skips report the normalized type used for the decision, and prompt and resource analyzers refuse a body that is already over the configured limit.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
